name: Havasu Falls
why: Down a side canyon of the Grand Canyon to Supai, the most remote village in the country, and to waterfalls of blue-green water over red rock.
book: Reservation only, sold by the Havasupai Tribe each February for the whole year (3 nights at the campground or lodge); no day hikes. Check in at Grand Canyon Caverns or Peach Springs the day before. The trailhead is Hualapai Hilltop, 100 km from Peach Springs.
water: Spring water at the campground; none on the 13 km from Hualapai Hilltop to Supai: carry 3 litres.
dangers: Flash floods in the canyon (2008 and 2018 evacuations): leave at any warning.
Heat in the bottom of the canyon; the climb out is 600 m with no shade.
The ladders and chains down to Mooney Falls are wet and steep.
turnaround: Climb out of the canyon early in the morning.
